decisions.reason: The second V is explicitly derived from the Hero V geometry and shares its proportions, so the revised arm relationship and silhouette necessarily apply to its derived geometry.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Thank you for continuing to explore this with me. I think I realized we've been interpreting some of the same words differently.

This round helped me realize that I don't think I'm looking for greater contrast between the two arms. I also don't want the left arm to become visually dominant or the right arm to become extremely thin.

Instead, I'd love to return to a supporting left arm paired with a right arm that extends just a little farther before it terminates. To me, the beauty comes from the relationship between those two gestures—not from emphasizing either one individually.

I think the overall silhouette is still the most important part. I'd rather continue refining a beautifully balanced composition than continue introducing new visual ideas. I think we're very close, and I'd love to keep refining this family rather than reinventing it.

Please refer back to the concept board because it still captures that balance better than anything we've explored since. I don't want to recreate it, but I do think it's the clearest expression of the feeling we're trying to achieve.

value_updates.arm_weight_relationship: balanced without a dominant left arm or extremely thin right arm
value_updates.composition_priority: balanced whole silhouette over emphasizing either arm

decisions.reason: The accent is derived from the Hero V geometry, but the source changes a two-arm relationship and does not establish how those arm-specific changes translate to the single accent form.
The source refines the Hero V's internal arm relationship and does not change the deferred E and L construction requirements.
The source changes V geometry but does not alter the closing V's established smaller, subordinate prominence relative to the Hero V.
The client provides geometric feedback but does not change the obligation to include design rationale with review rounds.
The source does not address spacing, kerning, or the unified reading of the full wordmark.
The source changes black-and-white Hero V geometry without modifying the deferred champagne material treatment.
The Hero V geometry decision is unrelated to the required file formats for viewable proof attachments.
